races.name: Ray And Eileen Mclean Memorial EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Jw 4x4 Northallerton Irish EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Heineken 0% Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Hover On The Wind
runners_data.note: Six-year-old with two recent wins on Good ground over this trip and solid Paul Midgley stable form; naturally a hold-up horse who will want to come late, but the crowded rear means he is likely to race closer to midfield than ideal, softening the impact of his finishing kick.
runners_data.comment: Hover On The Wind has back-to-back wins in his recent starts but tumbled to seventh last time out, and ranked eighth of nine on our figures he faces a stiff ask here; has run over today's trip and going, and 28 days off should have him fresh.

runners_data.name: Managing Director
runners_data.note: One of the two confirmed pace-setters, with a good-ground win at this trip and PJ McDonald in the saddle; the danger is a head-to-head battle with Equity Law draining his reserves, and a tendency to find little when pressed in past form at softer tracks is worth noting.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out suggests Managing Director is knocking on the door, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions; carrying 128 lb from stall two, the main risk is whether that weight blunts his finishing effort when it matters most.

runners_data.name: Our Absent Friends
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old prominent runner with a recent course win over this trip on Good ground and capable Shane Gray; the veteran profile is a concern for consistency but the style fit for this race shape is excellent if he can slot just behind the duelling front-runners.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of nine on our figures and officially rated just 69, Our Absent Friends is hard to fancy despite a win last time out; he has run over today's trip and going before, but five inconsistent efforts in his last six starts make that recent victory hard to trust.

runners_data.name: Winchurch
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby has a runner who has won twice recently including over this trip, and Tom Eaves partners a horse who can race from a hold-up position but is capable of being more prominent; the last run was a disappointing 0, but the two wins before that and recent trainer form (1/22 T14) suggest a revival is not out of the question.
runners_data.comment: Winchurch has winning form in recent starts, with victories two, four, and six starts back, though he was unplaced last time out; he has run over today's trip and going, but a struggling trainer at just 5% recently gives cause for pause.

runners_data.name: Rock Of England
runners_data.note: Three wins from five runs on Good ground over five furlongs mark him out as a course-and-distance specialist for Paul Midgley; a natural hold-up horse who is squeezed toward midfield by the volume of closers in this field, meaning his preferred late run may be compressed — style fit is marginally discounted as a result.
runners_data.comment: Ranked seventh of nine on our figures, Rock Of England is hard to fancy at the weights despite a lively recent record that includes a win two starts back; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 13 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Equity Law
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's five winners in the last 14 days gives this confirmed front-runner strong yard backing, and a recent Good-ground win over this trip with headgear noted; the key risk is whether Managing Director pushes him into an unsustainable early duel rather than allowing him to control the tempo.
runners_data.comment: Equity Law won last time out and was second two starts back, giving him a fine run of recent form, though 54 days off the track and a burden of 130 lb from stall 8 are factors to weigh against him here.

runners_data.name: Moulin Booj
runners_data.note: Highest official rating in the field at OR 81, recent win on Good ground over this trip, and Daniel Tudhope — one of the shrewdest judges of pace in the north — takes the ride; the three-day turnaround is short but George Scott has fired in two winners from 12 runners in the last fortnight, and the form profile makes him the obvious threat from behind.
runners_data.comment: Moulin Booj arrives on the back of a win last time out and a second two starts back, giving him a sharp recent profile that marks him out as a leading threat, though the quick three-day turnaround is the obvious question mark over whether he can back it up at his best.

runners_data.name: Accrual
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's five winners in 14 days speaks to a yard in form, and this five-year-old has a course win on Good ground; the sim-going record of only 1/15 comparable runs is a significant drag on confidence, and the form string includes a U (unseated) alongside moderate figures, making the talent harder to trust despite the recent trainer trajectory.
runners_data.comment: Accrual returns just 13 days after a winning effort, has run over today's trip and going, and his rating of 84 underlines his claims as a leading threat; the main risk is that fifth two starts back hints at inconsistency.

runners_data.name: Emerald Harmony
runners_data.note: Paul Midgley's third runner in the race and another natural hold-up horse forced to operate closer to midfield by the volume of rear-of-field types in the field; the recent form shows a five-timer sequence with a win on Good ground, but the redistribution out of his preferred closing role tempers expectations, and the stable's overall T14 figures (0/17) are uninspiring.
runners_data.comment: Emerald Harmony shaped with real promise when third two starts back and runner-up three starts back, and at 20 days since her last outing she arrives here in solid order, with experience of today's trip and going working in her favour from stall three.

races.paceDynamic: Equity Law and Managing Director are the two confirmed front-runners and will clash for early supremacy over Thirsk's straight five furlongs, creating a genuinely contested pace rather than a soft lead for either. On Good turf this is unlikely to be suicidal, but two horses fighting for the same real estate will stretch the field early and ensure an honest gallop that compresses the usual advantage front-runners enjoy on this course. That dynamic shifts the balance toward horses who can travel prominently in behind the duel and sustain their run to the line — the classic prominent-to-midfield profile that can sit just off the heat and pick up the pieces. Three genuine hold-up horses — Hover On The Wind, Rock Of England, and Emerald Harmony — are redistributed into the midfield graphic because this pace-heavy field leaves no clean late-running lane; all three are likely to be closer to the action than their natural style preference and their closing kick may be blunted by positional compromise.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Duel, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Equity Law and Managing Director fight hard early and the disputed lead sets up the race perfectly for a horse tracking just off the pace.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners press each other throughout, ensuring a true-run race where any horse able to sit a length or two off the pace in a prominent position gets a slingshot run to the line; Thirsk's flat five furlongs rewards those who travel well and sustain rather than those who quicken from deep. Our Absent Friends and Winchurch — both able to sit prominently — are the profiles that profit most if they can find a position just off the leaders.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two pace horses breaks cleaner and the other settles early, allowing a single horse to control tempo and steal a decisive advantage.
scenarios.body: Either Equity Law or Managing Director gains the upper hand within the first furlong and is allowed to bowl along unchallenged, converting the early pressure into a race-shaping solo lead; on Good ground over five furlongs at Thirsk a front-runner who avoids a war and dictates can be very hard to reel in. Equity Law, who has course and good-ground form, is the likelier beneficiary given Tim Easterby's strong recent strike rate and David Allan's familiarity with the track.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace duel burns out both Equity Law and Managing Director in the final furlong, leaving a window for the deepest runners.
scenarios.body: A genuinely hot pace could see both front-runners tying up close home, theoretically opening the door for horses coming from behind; however, this scenario is tempered by the fact that Rock Of England, Hover On The Wind, and Emerald Harmony — the three most natural closers — are all competing out of their ideal position and may not generate the clean late run needed to fully capitalise. Moulin Booj, who has course-winning form and is ridden by Daniel Tudhope, is the strongest candidate if a late closer is to strike.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the race becomes disorganised early and a horse sitting middle-to-rear finds an unexpected gap up the centre of the track.
scenarios.body: This is the lowest-probability outcome but not impossible on a flat straight track where gaps appear mid-race; a horse like Accrual, who has a recent win on Good ground and is ridden by William Pyle, could find daylight if the pace horses drift. The scenario is constrained by the number of hold-up types forced into similar positions, meaning interference and traffic problems are as likely as a clean passage.

watchPoints.text: Equity Law vs Managing Director — watch the first two furlongs closely; if both horses are hard at it by halfway the front two could tie up and compromise both their chances, radically altering the race shape.

Rock Of England, Hover On The Wind, and Emerald Harmony — three natural closers all jostling for the same rear-of-field position; traffic and interference in the final two furlongs is a real risk if they all need daylight at the same time.

Moulin Booj — three-day turnaround is unusually quick for a six-year-old handicapper; watch market moves at the track to see whether Tudhope's booking signals confidence the horse is fully wound up after such a tight gap.

Our Absent Friends — an eight-year-old winning on this course recently is not a red flag at this level, but watch whether Shane Gray can slot him into a prominent position early; if he gets buried in the pack his chance is significantly reduced given his age and the pace of this race.

races.name: Andrew Seaton Celebration Cup Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Enchant
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced Burke three-year-old who won her only start on Good ground, making a 61-day absence and just two career runs genuine unknowns; James Doyle takes the ride which is an upgrade in quality, and her style is unclassified — she could race anywhere — but the unknown ceiling cuts both ways.
runners_data.comment: Returned a winner two starts back but sixth last time out, and our figures put her well below the level required here; the 61-day absence adds further doubt, though she has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Return Of The Gods
runners_data.note: Bethell's confirmed front-runner won over course and distance on Good ground and Tudhope is a strong partner; at OR=79 he is the highest-rated runner with genuine positional control, and his ability to get an uncontested lead is the defining tactical factor of this entire race.
runners_data.comment: Winner two starts back and a close second three starts back, Return Of The Gods arrives fit on a 20-day break with experience over today's trip and the backing of a trainer firing at 31% in the past fortnight; the fourth last time out is a minor query, but his overall profile makes him the one to side with here.

runners_data.name: Zarvali
runners_data.note: Roger Fell's hold-up operator has a strong record at 7f on Good ground including a win, though his last run showed a drop to tenth suggesting inconsistency; Oisin Orr takes over in the saddle and the seven-day turnaround is brisk, so fitness is not a concern but he needs the pace to be strong.

runners_data.name: Substance
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse whose best form on Good ground came at 7f, winning over a mile on Good at his most recent relevant run; the 70-day absence and the switch to a flat track from a more varied route makes him one to assess in-running — headgear worn throughout his career.
runners_data.comment: Substance landed a win three starts back and franked that with a third last time out, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions; the main risk is a 70-day absence returning fresh on 131 lb.

runners_data.name: Raging Raj
runners_data.note: Herrington's prominent racer won at 7f on Good ground and has placed at 8f, suggesting the trip is well within range; Tom Eaves retains the ride after a 20-day break, and his natural position just off the pace means he should travel comfortably in the slipstream of Return Of The Gods.
runners_data.comment: Raging Raj has the experience of today's trip and conditions in his favour, and a winner two starts back shows he can find the track, but a fifth last time out and 130 lb to carry are the checks on expectations here.

runners_data.name: Shadow Run
runners_data.note: Scott Dixon's horse is a genuine hold-up type by style and form — placed twice at 7f on Good — but the crowded rear of the field has pushed his map position to midfield; the STYLE_FIT tag reflects he is unlikely to get the true back-of-the-field position his running demands, which tempers confidence in a strong finish.
runners_data.comment: Shadow Run has been placed twice in his last five starts — second last time out and a second four starts back — and he steps up with experience over today's trip and going under 127 lb, yet winless in recent starts remains the concern.

runners_data.name: Derrygarran Lad
runners_data.note: Julie Camacho's unbeaten maiden — 2-from-3 placed in all starts — steps into handicap company for the first time with a clean record but limited evidence; the headgear worn previously may assist concentration, and Sexton retains the ride, though the step into handicap competition at 7f on Good is a genuine test.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts despite a pair of seconds and a third, Derrygarran Lad finds himself ranked bottom on our figures here, and with a speed rating of 64 he faces a stiff ask, though he has run over today's trip before and returns 26 days fresh.

runners_data.name: Indefensible
runners_data.note: Ollie Pears' prominent racer has an excellent record on Good ground at 7f including a win, multiple places, and consistent effort; Harry Russell takes over the ride and OR=71 looks potentially lenient if he recaptures that 7f Good win form — his trainer's 0-from-8 record in the last 14 days is a mild flag.
runners_data.comment: Indefensible won last time out and has run over today's distance and going before, giving him solid claims, though he has been third on two of his last three starts and our rating ranks him sixth of eight in this field.

races.paceDynamic: Return Of The Gods is the confirmed front-runner here, and on a flat, fair track at Thirsk in Good conditions, he should be able to stride into a comfortable early lead and control the tempo without being seriously challenged for supremacy. Raging Raj and Indefensible carry prominent styles and will press for position behind him, but neither appears likely to seriously contest Return Of The Gods for the front rail, meaning the pace is likely to be honest rather than scorching. The closers — Zarvali, Substance, and the repositioned Shadow Run — will need a strong gallop to make ground effectively over 7f, and if Return Of The Gods dictates a measured pace, horses racing prominently or just off the pace in the first three or four will be best served by this shape. This race shape clearly favours prominent racers and those able to travel close to the pace, as a single unchallenged front-runner on a flat track over 7f in Good ground typically sets up a race won from the front two or three. Shadow Run, a true hold-up horse, has been mapped to midfield because the field holds more genuine rear-runners than the race shape can accommodate at the back, and Return Of The Gods is by far the most likely to actually dictate from the front.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Return Of The Gods Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Return Of The Gods breaks cleanly and controls the tempo unchallenged from flag to finish.
scenarios.body: Tudhope on Return Of The Gods sets a measured, comfortable gallop, reaching the straight with a length or two in hand and enough in reserve to kick clear inside the final furlong; horses racing prominently just off his back — Raging Raj and Indefensible — are best placed to capitalise if he weakens.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Storm Late
scenarios.trigger: If Return Of The Gods goes off too hard early and the true hold-up horses get a strong pace to aim at.
scenarios.body: A fast early gallop from Return Of The Gods stretches the field and sets up a potent late finish, allowing Zarvali and Substance, who both have form at 7f on Good ground, to come home strongly through tired rivals in the final 2f.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Grind It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Return Of The Gods fades and the race becomes a battle between the chasing prominent horses from 2f out.
scenarios.body: Indefensible, with strong similar-going form including a win at this track and trip, and Raging Raj, who won over 7f on Good ground, take over from the weakening leader and grind out a result between them in a modest sprint finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Lightly Raced Improver Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Enchant, whose lightly raced profile masks untapped ability, shows a sharp upturn on her handicap debut over this trip.
scenarios.body: Enchant, trained by K.R. Burke who fires juveniles and three-year-olds into form off breaks, races prominently under James Doyle and uses her unknown ceiling to outclass rivals rated just slightly higher; her 2-from-2 record on Good ground is the key flag.

watchPoints.text: Return Of The Gods — Tudhope's use of the front and the pace he sets in the first 2f will dictate the outcome of the entire race; if he goes unchallenged, the race is likely already over.

Shadow Run — a genuine hold-up horse unable to get to the back of this field as intended; if Luke Morris is forced to race in midfield out of position, the STYLE_FIT concern becomes a live threat to his effectiveness in the closing stages.
Indefensible — the trainer's 0-from-8 strike rate in the last 14 days is a meaningful context point despite the horse's strong personal form profile at this trip and going.

Enchant — the K.R. Burke yard's record with lightly-raced three-year-olds coming back off a 60-day break and stepping into handicap company is worth monitoring in the market; sharp market moves for this runner would be significant given the unknown ceiling.

Zarvali — the seven-day turnaround following a run that produced a tenth-place finish is an unusual pattern; watch early in-running whether Orr can get him to travel with more rhythm than his last effort suggested.

races.name: Malton Marquees Racing Through The Summer Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Roaring Ralph
runners_data.note: Has won twice at 8f on good ground in recent form (wins at Nottingham and Carlisle) and his prominent style suits racing just off a single leader; cheekpieces fitted and Sean Kirrane takes the ride for the in-form Michael Dods yard.
runners_data.comment: Roaring Ralph has won three times in his last six starts, but he has a bit to find on our figures, ranked 11 of 15, and an unplaced effort last time out does little to inspire confidence, even if he has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Style Of Life
runners_data.note: The lone genuine front-runner here, boasting two wins from five runs at 8f on good ground and uncontested control of the pace; 91 days off is the key question but Harriet Bethell's 1/8 recent record suggests the yard is not firing at full volume.

runners_data.name: Bloodsweatandtyres
runners_data.note: Prominent runner whose best form has come on Tapeta (one win from five on turf, none on good) and that going concern is material here; Ben Robinson takes over but this looks a tough spot to reverse a losing sequence on this surface.
runners_data.comment: Bloodsweatandtyres has experience of today's distance and going, and a win four starts back gives him a recent winning benchmark; at 134 lb from stall 10, the weight burden after three below-par efforts since that victory is the concern.

runners_data.name: Military Leader
runners_data.note: Consistent placed horse with five of his last six runs at 8f on good going producing wins or seconds; Paul Mulrennan's experience in a scrappy prominent bunch is a real asset and the horse's pattern of holding his position under pressure suits this shape well.
runners_data.comment: Military Leader has placed in each of his last four starts, including two wins in his last six, and has run over today's trip and going — a consistent profile. However, six days between runs is a quick turnaround, and 133 lb is a stern burden to overcome.

runners_data.name: Alessia Fernanda
runners_data.note: A hold-up mare who has been in the frame twice at 8f on good going recently; Zak Wheatley is apprentice-claimed and the horse needs a clear run late, which is achievable in a race where the prominent group may tie themselves in knots.
runners_data.comment: Placed second last time out after a mid-table spell, Alessia Fernanda brings distance and going experience and rates 3 lb above her official mark, yet her record in recent starts shows inconsistency, and 132 lb from stall nine will test her here.

runners_data.name: Harswell Ruby
runners_data.note: Prominent type with a consistent placed record at 8f on good ground — four of last five runs — but has yet to win at this trip and her higher finishing positions in smaller fields may flatter her here in a 15-runner heat.
runners_data.comment: Harswell Ruby arrives in decent nick on a 16-day turnaround, and her second three starts back gives her a strong claims against this field; drawing stall one and carrying 132 lb while yet to win in recent starts is the main concern.

runners_data.name: Donna Nook
runners_data.note: Has won at 8f on good and placed several times at the trip; Daniel Tudhope is a major plus in a race where positioning will matter, and tongue-tie and visor suggest connections are alert to keeping her focussed in a big field.
runners_data.comment: Donna Nook catches the eye on our ratings as the second-ranked runner in this field, and she has experience of both today's trip and going to call on, stepping back up having won four starts back. The worry is that three subsequent fourths suggest she may struggle to convert.

runners_data.name: Green Pursuit
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who has run exclusively over 7f on good ground recently and has not been seen for 61 days; stepping up to 8f for the first time in this form cycle is an unresolved question, and the layoff adds further doubt.
runners_data.comment: Third two starts back represents Green Pursuit's best recent showing, and he has run over today's trip and going, giving him necessary experience heading in; yet to score in his last five starts, though our rating of 84 marks him the one to beat from stall 12 fresh off a 61-day absence.

runners_data.name: Jesmond Dawn
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who has placed at 8f on good ground multiple times including a win last time out at this trip; Oliver Stammers is an inexperienced rider in a notably competitive prominent group — rider quality in the scrimmage is a real risk here.
runners_data.comment: Jesmond Dawn ranks 12th of 15 on our figures, making him hard to fancy, and he finished fifth last time out; the win came two starts back. He has run over today's trip and going, and draws stall two carrying 130 lb.

runners_data.name: Up The Jazz
runners_data.note: Finished second and third at 8f on good ground in his last five and has genuine mid-to-hold-up versatility; Ethan Tindall's 5lb claim is useful and the horse's wide-run option could become a genuine asset if the inner is congested.
runners_data.comment: Up The Jazz showed well when winning three starts back and was a close second two starts ago, but seventh last time out clouds his claims; he has run over today's distance and going before, and 20 days since that below-par effort leaves him needing to bounce back from stall four off 129 lb.

runners_data.name: Degale
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with three of his last four runs at 8f on good going placing him in the frame, but finishing positions of 3, 5, 8 suggest he is running into these without winning; Oisin Orr is a significant jockey booking that raises the competitive ceiling.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Degale does at least bring distance and going experience to this assignment and steps in here on a fresh 15-day break, though carrying 127 lb from stall six and ranking tenth of fifteen on ratings suggests he faces a stiff ask.

runners_data.name: Mount King
runners_data.note: Strong recent form — two wins in the last six runs including a win at 8f on good — and Tim Easterby's yard is at the peak of its 14-day stats (5/69); however, his true hold-up style means he is likely to find himself a length or two further forward than ideal in this single-pace-setter race, which costs him his natural finish.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 14 of 15 on our figures, Mount King makes it hard to build a case despite a second last time out and a winner two starts back; he has run over today's trip and going, but at 125 lb from stall seven, better efforts look needed to trouble these rivals.

runners_data.name: Travis
runners_data.note: Won at 7f on good and has placed third three times in recent runs; his true closer's profile is compromised by the redistribution — in a 15-runner field with only one front-runner, he risks being shuffled into an unfamiliar midfield berth that neither suits his style nor rewards Geoffrey Harker's patient approach.
runners_data.comment: Travis has placed third in three consecutive starts and was a winner four starts back, but two unplaced efforts in his last six suggest inconsistency holds him back; he has run over today's trip and going, carries 122 lb from stall 8, and returns on a sharp 14-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Palmarian
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's runner has strong recent form at 8f on good including a win, and James Sullivan has ridden him effectively; his natural rear-of-field style is his weapon, but the redistribution effect in this race shape means he is unlikely to find the isolation at the back that allows a clean late run.
runners_data.comment: Palmarian has won once in his last six starts, with a second two starts back offset by a string of poor efforts either side, and ranked 13 of 15 on our figures he faces a stiff ask here; has run over today's trip and going, and 22 days between runs suggests he arrives reasonably fresh.

runners_data.name: Miss Willows
runners_data.note: A seven-year-old hold-up mare returning after 59 days off with a form string that contains wins at 7f and 8f on good; the layoff is significant and Luke Morris will find it hard to manufacture a genuine late run from out the back in a field where the true hold-up positions are already crowded.
runners_data.comment: Miss Willows won one in her last five starts but has been unplaced in two of the three since, and ranked last of 15 on our figures she faces a stiff task; a runner-up last time out and experience of today's trip and going are the only crumbs of comfort.

races.paceDynamic: Style Of Life is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with only one horse genuinely wanting to lead, she is likely to settle into an uncontested rhythm from the gates and control tempo through the early part of this mile on good ground at Thirsk. Behind her, a cluster of six prominent-seeking horses — Roaring Ralph, Bloodsweatandtyres, Military Leader, Harswell Ruby, Donna Nook and Jesmond Dawn — will jostle for the early positions two through six, creating genuine traffic compression between the two-furlong and three-furlong markers as they try to slot in behind a single leader. The field contains more hold-up and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate cleanly: Mount King, Travis, Palmarian and Miss Willows are true hold-up horses who are likely to find themselves racing further forward than ideal, diluting their late-run capacity. This race shape — one honest pace-setter controlling tempo in a sea of prominent horses — typically rewards horses with tactical speed who can travel close to the pace without getting squeezed, making prominent-to-midfield runners with proven good-ground form at this trip the primary beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Style Of Life controls, prominent win
scenarios.trigger: If Style Of Life dictates a measured, unchallenged tempo and the prominent scrimmage resolves without incident by the half-mile pole.
scenarios.body: Style Of Life sets a sustainable gallop that blunts the closers, and the horse best positioned just off the leader — with the tactical sharpness to pick her off in the final two furlongs — collects.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent scrimmage produces midfield winner
scenarios.trigger: If the six prominent horses crowd each other turning in, disrupting their own momentum and gifting a clear passage to a genuine midfield traveller.
scenarios.body: The jostling for positions two through six burns energy and causes interference, leaving a horse that settles mid-division to find a clean line at the two-furlong pole.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Style Of Life quickens, front-runner wins
scenarios.trigger: If Style Of Life proves better than her OR suggests and converts her uncontested lead into a front-running victory by putting the race to bed from the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: Having been off 91 days she arrives fresh and her good-ground record at this trip is strong; if her handler has her spot-on she can control every yard and hold on as the field gets into gear too late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: True hold-up horses pounce late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final quarter-mile and those redistributed hold-up types somehow secure wider berths and produce genuine late runs.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely shape because Mount King, Travis, Palmarian and Miss Willows are all racing out of role and are unlikely to find the clear daylight a hold-up finish requires in a 15-runner handicap on a flat track.

watchPoints.text: Style Of Life (J: P J McDonald) — watch whether she travels smoothly to the front unchallenged at the flag; if Roaring Ralph or Bloodsweatandtyres press her early, tempo increases and the race shape shifts entirely.

The prominent group of six (Roaring Ralph, Bloodsweatandtyres, Military Leader, Harswell Ruby, Donna Nook, Jesmond Dawn) — watch for crowding and checking between the 3f and 2f markers where Thirsk's flat, straight run-in concentrates traffic danger most acutely.

Mount King (J: David Allan) — watch his position at the start; if he is forced to race much further forward than his natural hold-up style, his closing kick is negated and his form figures become largely irrelevant to the outcome.

Jesmond Dawn (J: Oliver Stammers) — an inexperienced apprentice in a congested prominent group is a combination to monitor; if Stammers gets squeezed or loses his position in the early stages, the horse's chance effectively ends before the race begins.

Green Pursuit (J: Dale Swift) — stepping up from 7f to 8f for the first time in this campaign after 61 days off; watch the early market move for any stable confidence signal, as an unexposed mile trip plus a layoff makes him either an unknown commodity or a well-aimed runner.

races.name: Birra Moretti Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Prince Achille
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up performer with a consistent placed record across 10-11f on standard and good ground, Jack Garritty takes over after 148 days off and the return to form will be key — five consecutive placed efforts suggest reliability without a win since well before this campaign, and his ability to travel close to a slow pace is his main tactical asset here.
runners_data.comment: Prince Achille rates ahead of his rivals on our figures and has experience of today's trip and conditions, making him a live threat despite carrying 136 lb; the concern is he is winless in his last five starts and returns after 148 days off.

runners_data.name: Halimede
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's three-year-old has won her last two outings over 12-13f on stamina tracks and good ground, giving her strong claims on trip and going, but she is a natural hold-up type that has been placed on the front end here purely by default — she fades in the finish according to her profile flag, which is a genuine concern if she has to do all the work from the front over 1m4f on just six days' rest.
runners_data.comment: Halimede arrives on the back of back-to-back wins and, with only six days between runs, fitness is not in question; she has run over today's trip and her overall profile makes her our pick despite carrying 135 lb.

runners_data.name: Recobella
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby's five-year-old owns a win over 10f on good and multiple placings at 10-12f, and Tom Kiely-Marshall's 5lb claim is a meaningful weight relief, but her true running style is hold-up and she has been shifted to a midfield slot only because the race has an excess of horses who want to come from behind — racing further forward than ideal tempers confidence in her ability to produce her best.
runners_data.comment: Recobella ran a fine second last time out and was a winner two starts back, showing she retains form, and her experience over today's trip and going underlines her claims; the main risk is the quick four-day turnaround.

races.paceDynamic: Halimede is the only horse mapped to the front and, while a natural hold-up type redistributed to lead, her two most recent wins came over 12-13f at a stamina-testing pace and Sir Mark Prescott's handlers will almost certainly allow her to stride on uncontested from the gate. With just three runners and no genuine front-runner in the field, Halimede is likely to dictate at a controlled, measured gallop on good ground over 1m4f, setting a pace that suits those who can track and pick up rather than deep closers. Prince Achille and Recobella are both true hold-up horses — Recobella mapped to midfield due to the field's composition — meaning both will sit behind Halimede and rely on a strong enough pace to create a winning run-in rather than the slow-burn tempo that a lone leader often imposes. This race shape strongly favours a horse that can track the modest pace closely and produce a sustained finish, rather than a true deep closer needing a strong gallop to deliver from the back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Halimede controls unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Halimede strides to the front unchallenged and dictates a controlled tempo, conserving enough for the final 2f.
scenarios.body: Halimede sets a comfortable pace over 1m4f on good ground, and with no rival pressing her she can dictate the fractions to suit her stamina; her two recent wins at 12-13f on similar ground confirm she sees out this trip strongly when fresh.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tracker pounces late
scenarios.trigger: If Halimede's pace is just fast enough to stretch the field and the closer tracking her can deliver a sustained challenge inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A moderate but not wholly slow tempo still creates enough of a test that the horse sitting second can wear down Halimede close home; Prince Achille, who has been placed consistently at 10f, is the likeliest beneficiary if he can hold a tracking position.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Recobella powers through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely testing enough to find out Halimede late and Recobella can deliver from further back than her natural position.
scenarios.body: Recobella arrives from the widest margin but is racing out of her ideal hold-up role mapped to midfield, which reduces the purity of her run; she has won at 10f on good and soft so has the class, but depends on a scenario where Halimede ties up.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Halimede fades, closers fail
scenarios.trigger: If Halimede's known tendency to fade in the finish is triggered by even a modest solo effort and no other runner is positioned well enough to capitalise.
scenarios.body: With all three horses essentially hold-up or reluctant front-runners, none may be ideally placed to pounce decisively, producing a messy finish where margins are small and positional luck decides the result; Prince Achille's consistency at 10f could eke out a minor placing.

watchPoints.text: Halimede's known tendency to fade in the finish is a critical flag — watch whether she ties up approaching the final furlong having led throughout without cover.
Prince Achille returns after 148 days off; watch his early movement and whether Garritty attempts to close the gap on Halimede quickly enough to be a live threat entering the final bend.
Recobella has run just four days ago — watch her market drift or support in the ring as a guide to whether connections are confident she has recovered sufficiently for this quick turnaround.

With only three runners and all effectively hold-up types, watch the early stages for whether any jockey actively contests the lead — if Halimede is not pressed she will control the entire race shape by default.
Good ground is confirmed throughout the card at Thirsk; watch for any late inspection or clerk-of-the-course update that could shift the going description ahead of this final race on the card.
